summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication on CentOS Stream 10: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only hot standbys receiving WAL via a dedicated 'replicator' role over scram-sha-256 auth (password generated on node1, transferred to node2/node3 via cluster SSH keys, never printed to the transcript except one accidental unredacted postgresql.auto.conf dump on node2 which is now known only in this transcript and not repeated in this report). Verified changes committed on the primary propagate to both standbys in near real time and that standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: each node was rebooted one at a time (node2, then node3, then node1 last) via `systemctl reboot`, preserving quorum throughout, with boot_id captured before/after each restart proving an actual reboot, and PostgreSQL/replication health confirmed recovered on every node afterward, including a final write on the primary that replicated to both standbys post-restart.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 and postgresql-contrib on node1, node2, node3 via dnf (epel-release added on node1 but appstream already had the package)
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes
Initialized the primary database on node1 and configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, max_replication_slots, hot_standby in postgresql.conf

Generated a random replication password on node1, created the 'replicator' ROLE WITH REPLICATION LOGIN, and added pg_hba.conf rules scoping replication and general access to the cluster subnet with scram-sha-256
Distributed the replication password file to node2/node3 over cluster-keypair SSH (not printed in chat)
Ran pg_basebackup -R from node1 on node2 and node3 to bootstrap standbys with standby.signal and primary_conninfo auto-configured
Started/enabled postgresql on node2 and node3 as standbys
Verified pg_stat_replication on primary shows both standbys streaming, and standbys report pg_is_in_recovery()=t and reject INSERTs
Inserted rows on the primary and confirmed propagation to both standbys via SELECT and LSN comparison
Captured boot_id and uptime -s baseline on all 3 nodes
Rebooted node2, then node3, then node1 sequentially (one at a time, preserving quorum), each via backgrounded systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled each node until exec was available again and confirmed boot_id changed on all three
Verified PostgreSQL service active and replication/recovery state restored on each node after its reboot
After node1 (primary) restart, inserted a new row and confirmed it replicated to both standbys

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured: node1 primary (writable), node2/node3 standbys (read-only)
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 and node3 in 'streaming' state; node2/node3 psql shows pg_is_in_recovery()=t and INSERT fails with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on primary visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Inserted streamed-row-2 on node1 primary; both node2 and node3 show the row with matching/advanced WAL replay LSN moments later

boot_id 4d842549-... captured on node3 prior to restart (from initial inspection)
